---
title: "Feature list"
---

Every feature column produced by
[feature computation](../how-to/compute-features-spikeglx.qmd), grouped by the family that
emits it. The columns and units below are those declared by the pandera schemas in
`ephysatlas.features`, which are what the code validates against.

Columns marked **\*** are optional or nullable: they are absent from older vintages, or
only produced when a specific option is enabled. Everything else is always present when
its family is computed.

## Families

| family | band | schema | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lf` | LF | `ModelLfFeatures` | lite install |
| `csd` | LF | `ModelCsdFeatures` | lite install |
| `ap` | AP | `ModelApFeatures` | lite install |
| `waveforms` | AP | `ModelSpikeFeatures` | `[full]` extra ([DARTsort](https://github.com/cwindolf/dartsort)) |

`ModelRawFeatures` is the union of all four plus `ModelChannelLayout` (56 columns), and is
the schema a complete raw feature table validates against. `ModelDenoisedFeatures` (54
columns) is the same with the spike block swapped for the
[spike-shape columns](#spike-shape-columns); a
denoised table written since `ephysatlas` 0.9.0 validates against it (tables before
`2026_W42` once their `*_csd_diff1` columns are renamed, as `read_features_from_disk`
does).

![The features at a glance: a schematic of each, its distribution over the IBL dataset, and what it is thought to reflect. The names follow an earlier vintage (`peak-val`, `trough-val`, ... are the landmark columns that the denoised table now remaps).](../figures/raw_to_features.png){.lightbox}

## Frequency bands

Every `psd_*` column integrates power over one of these bands, defined in
`ephysatlas.features.BANDS`:

| band | range (Hz) |
|---|---|
| `delta` | 0 – 4 |
| `theta` | 4 – 10 |
| `alpha` | 8 – 12 |
| `beta` | 15 – 30 |
| `gamma` | 30 – 90 |
| `lfp` | 0 – 90 |

`alpha` overlaps both `theta` and `beta`, and `lfp` spans the whole range — the bands are
not a partition, so the `psd_*` columns are not independent and do not sum to `psd_lfp`.

## Raw versus denoised units

Three features are **transformed by denoising** and returned in the transformed unit:

| column | raw unit | denoised unit | transform |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rms_lf` | V | dB rel. V | `20 · log10(x)` |
| `rms_ap` | V | dB rel. V | `20 · log10(x)` |
| `spike_count` | count/s | log2 (count/s) | `log2(x)`, with `0 → NaN` |

So `raw_ephys_features.pqt` has `rms_lf` around 1e-5 while
`raw_ephys_features_denoised.pqt` has it around −90. The unit column in the tables below
gives the **denoised** unit where a transform exists. A model trained on denoised features
expects the denoised unit — see [aggregate and denoise](../how-to/aggregate-and-denoise.qmd).

### `lf` — `ModelLfFeatures` (19 columns)

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `rms_lf` | dB rel. V | Root mean square of the LFP signal |
| `psd_lfp` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 0 – 90 Hz |
| `psd_delta` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 0 – 4 Hz |
| `psd_theta` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 4 – 10 Hz |
| `psd_alpha` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 8 – 12 Hz |
| `psd_beta` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 15 – 30 Hz |
| `psd_gamma` | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in the band 30 – 90 Hz |
| `psd_residual_lfp` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 0 – 90 Hz after removing the linear fit of the PSD decay in log-log space |
| `psd_residual_delta` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 0 – 4 Hz after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `psd_residual_theta` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 4 – 10 Hz after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `psd_residual_alpha` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 8 – 12 Hz after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `psd_residual_beta` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 15 – 30 Hz after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `psd_residual_gamma` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Power in 30 – 90 Hz after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `aperiodic_offset` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Y-intercept of the PSD-decay fit in log-log space |
| `aperiodic_exponent` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | Slope of the PSD-decay fit in log-log space |
| `decay_fit_error` * | dB rel. V²/Hz | RMS error of the PSD-decay fit |
| `decay_fit_r_squared` * | dimensionless | R² of the PSD-decay fit |
| `decay_n_peaks` * | count | Number of peaks detected in the residual after removing the PSD-decay fit |
| `rms_lf_no_car` * | dB rel. V | LFP RMS destriped **without** common-average referencing. Opt in via `LfParams(compute_rms_no_car=True)` |

The `psd_residual_*`, `aperiodic_*` and `decay_*` columns are the **spectral
parameterisation** features, computed with [specparam](https://specparam-tools.github.io/)
and introduced in vintage `2025_W39`. They are controlled by
`LfParams(decay_features=True)`, on by default. Vintages before `2025_W39` lack them
entirely — which matters, because every published region decoder requires them.

### `csd` — `ModelCsdFeatures` (14 columns)

The same measures computed on spatial differences of the LFP rather than the raw LFP:
the `*_csd` columns on the second difference (the current-source density proper) and
the `*_bpr` columns on the first difference between consecutive contacts of a column
(bipolar referencing). Both are Cadzow-denoised first and scaled by the tissue
conductivity and the intercontact distance, so their units are A/m³ and A/m². With
`CsdParams(scale=False)` they are raw differences in V and these units do not apply.

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `rms_lf_csd` | dB rel. A/m³ | Root mean square of the CSD signal |
| `psd_delta_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 0 – 4 Hz |
| `psd_theta_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 4 – 10 Hz |
| `psd_alpha_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 8 – 12 Hz |
| `psd_beta_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 15 – 30 Hz |
| `psd_gamma_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 30 – 90 Hz |
| `psd_lfp_csd` | dB rel. (A/m³)²/Hz | CSD power in 0 – 90 Hz |
| `rms_lf_bpr` * | dB rel. A/m² | Root mean square of the bipolar-referenced (BPR) signal |
| `psd_delta_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 0 – 4 Hz |
| `psd_theta_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 4 – 10 Hz |
| `psd_alpha_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 8 – 12 Hz |
| `psd_beta_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 15 – 30 Hz |
| `psd_gamma_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 30 – 90 Hz |
| `psd_lfp_bpr` * | dB rel. (A/m²)²/Hz | BPR power in 0 – 90 Hz |

The `*_bpr` columns were called `*_csd_diff1` before vintage `2026_W42`.
`ephysatlas.data.read_features_from_disk` renames them when it reads an older table
(`data.LEGACY_FEATURE_RENAMES`).

### `ap` — `ModelApFeatures` (3 columns)

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `rms_ap` | dB rel. V | Root mean square of the AP signal |
| `cor_ratio` | dimensionless | Median zero-lag cross-correlation with neighbouring channels, over the zero-lag autocorrelation |
| `channel_labels` | code | Channel quality label — see below |

`channel_labels` is a small integer code, not a measurement:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Good channel |
| `1` | Dead — low coherence or amplitude |
| `2` | Noisy |
| `3` | Outside the brain |

Anything greater than `0` is a bad channel. `read_features_from_disk` derives a boolean
`outside` column from `channel_labels == 3`, and the region decoder consumes both.

### `waveforms` — `ModelSpikeFeatures` (18 columns)

Requires the `[full]` extra. Twelve columns are shared with the
[spike-shape schema](#spike-shape-columns) (they live on
`ModelSpikeSharedFeatures`):

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `spike_count` | log2 (count/s) | Mean spike rate across snippets (nulls counted as 0), log2-transformed |
| `alpha_mean` | native | Mean spike "brightness", from the spike-localisation step |
| `alpha_std` | native | Standard deviation of the spike brightness |
| `polarity` | dimensionless | Sum of per-spike polarities divided by the number of spikes |
| `tip_val` | V | Waveform tip amplitude |
| `depolarisation_slope` | V/s | Slope of the line crossing the tip and peak points |
| `repolarisation_slope` | V/s | Slope of the line crossing the peak and trough points |
| `recovery_slope` | V/s | Slope of the line crossing the trough and recovery points |
| `spatial_spread_um` * | µm | Amplitude-weighted mean distance of the multi-channel waveform's neighbour channels from the peak channel |
| `spatial_spread_um_std` * | µm | Its standard deviation across the channel's spikes |
| `slowness_s_per_m` * | s/m | Signed slowness (inverse apparent velocity) of the waveform along the probe axis |
| `slowness_s_per_m_std` * | s/m | Its standard deviation across the channel's spikes |

and six are the raw waveform landmarks, relative to the extracted waveform window:

![(a) The waveform landmarks — tip, peak, trough, recovery and the half-peak width — and the depolarisation, repolarisation and recovery slopes between them. (b) The same landmarks (stars) found on four recorded waveforms (blue); the black line is the half-peak level.](../figures/waveform_points.png){.lightbox}

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `peak_time_secs` | s | Time to the waveform peak |
| `peak_val` | V | Peak amplitude |
| `trough_time_secs` | s | Time to the waveform trough |
| `trough_val` | V | Trough amplitude |
| `tip_time_secs` | s | Time to the waveform tip |
| `recovery_time_secs` | s | Recovery time |

The four spread and slowness columns are nullable: NaN wherever too few neighbour channels
have a usable value, and the `_std` columns are NaN on a channel with fewer than two
qualifying spikes (sample standard deviation). `alpha_mean` / `alpha_std` stay in
DARTsort's native localisation units.

::: {.callout-note}
The six landmark columns carry no `description` in the pandera schema itself, and the
four timing ones no unit — the descriptions above come from the `ModelSpikeFeatures`
class docstring. Read `ephysatlas.features.spikes` if you need the exact definition.
:::

Waveform geometry is 121 samples with the trough at sample 42. Two boundaries make
waveform features incomparable across them:

- **0.7.0, the DARTsort 0.5 migration:** detections rose about 9.5 % and amplitudes came
  out about 10 % smaller.
- **0.9.0:** amplitudes are in **volts**. Before, they were in DARTsort's per-channel RMS
  units (amplitudes and slopes alike), and `spike_count` was a per-snippet count rather
  than a rate. Tables from `2026_W39` on use the new units.

### Spike-shape columns — `ModelSpikeShapeFeatures` (16 columns) {#spike-shape-columns}

The **denoised** tables replace the six landmark columns with four interpretable ones,
computed from them (`aggregation.apply_waveform_remap`); the twelve shared columns pass
through:

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `spike_width_secs` | s | Trough-to-peak duration: `trough_time_secs − peak_time_secs` |
| `predepolarisation_width_secs` | s | Tip-to-peak duration: `peak_time_secs − tip_time_secs` |
| `spike_amplitude` | V | Overall amplitude: `trough_val − peak_val` |
| `peak_to_trough_ratio_log` | dimensionless | `log(|peak_val / trough_val|)`: shape asymmetry, independent of amplitude |

The raw tables (`raw_ephys_features.pqt`) keep the landmark columns.
`remap_waveform_shape_features` applies the same transform to a table you hold, and
`remap_waveform_shape_features_volume` to an
[encoding volume](../how-to/load-encoding-volume.qmd).

### Channel metadata — `ModelChannelLayout`

Always present, from the recording geometry rather than a feature family.

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `axial_um` | µm | Distance along the probe length (depth) |
| `lateral_um` | µm | Distance across the probe width |

The full `channels.pqt` table, as published in `ea_active/2026_W42`
(402,816 channels across 1,049 probes):

| column | unit | description |
|---|---|---|
| `pid` | — | Probe insertion id (index level 0) |
| `channel` | index | Channel index (index level 1) |
| `x`, `y`, `z` | **m** | Resolved histology coordinates from Bregma — **metres**, see below |
| `x_target`, `y_target`, `z_target` | **m** | Target coordinates from the best Alyx trajectory — **metres**, see below |
| `axial_um` | µm | Distance along the probe length (depth). Observed 20 – 3840 |
| `lateral_um` | µm | Distance across the probe width. Observed 11 – 59 |
| `acronym` | — | Brain region acronym, Allen mapping |
| `atlas_id` | — | Allen structure id |
| `labels` | code | Channel quality label. ~34 % null in `2026_W42` |
| `rawInd` | index | Original channel index from the source. Descriptive only |
| `shank` | index | Shank number |
| `probe_model` | — | Probe part number from SpikeGLX (`imDatPrb_pn`), e.g. `PRB_1_4_0480_1` |
| `referencing_scheme` | — | `external`, `tip`, `ground` or `on_shank`, from SpikeGLX `imroTbl` |

In `2026_W39` and `2026_W42` every column except `labels` is fully populated. Older vintages are
sparser: in `2026_W37`, `labels` was ~99 % null, `rawInd` / `shank` / `probe_model` /
`referencing_scheme` ~94 % (populated only where SpikeGLX metadata was available at
aggregation time), and the `*_target` columns ~50 %.

`distance_to_tip_um` is declared `Optional` in `ChannelDataFrameSchema` but is not present
in any current `ea_active` vintage.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two different length units in one table

**Coordinates are in metres. Probe geometry is in micrometres.**

| columns | unit |
|---|---|
| `x`, `y`, `z`, `x_target`, `y_target`, `z_target` | **metres** (from Bregma, IBL convention) |
| `axial_um`, `lateral_um`, `distance_to_tip_um` | **micrometres** |

Practical consequence: the plotting functions want the **µm** pair
(`lateral_um`, `axial_um`), while the
[spatial encoder](../how-to/predict-features-from-position.qmd) wants the **metre**
triple. Passing µm to the encoder places every channel outside the brain and returns
meaningless predictions with no error.

Verified against `ea_active/2026_W37`: reprojecting `x`/`y`/`z` through
`AllenAtlas.get_labels` — a metres API — reproduces the table's own `acronym` column for
**100%** of a 4,000-channel random sample; reading the same values as micrometres
reproduces 2.7%. The observed range, ±0.008, is a mouse brain in metres.

`ChannelDataFrameSchema`, `ModelHistologyResolved` and `ModelHistologyPlanned` declared
`raw_unit: "um"` for all six coordinate columns before 0.9.0. That was wrong and is
corrected. All six also name the coordinate space in their `description`. Planned and
resolved coordinates share a frame and differ only by insertion error.
:::

The `*_target` columns come from `feature_computation.add_target_coordinates`. It queries
Alyx trajectories up to provenance 50 and takes the best one the insertion has, in the
order of `feature_computation.PROVENANCE_PREFERENCE`:

1. `Micro-manipulator` (provenance 30)
2. else `Planned` (10)
3. else `Histology track` (50)

A micro-manipulator or planned trajectory is converted from the needles (in-vivo) atlas
into Allen space, with the 5° pitch correction. A histology track is already in Allen
space and is used as is. An insertion with none of the three raises `ValueError`.

## Programmatic access

Do not hardcode a feature list — derive it:

```python
import ephysatlas.features

# All feature columns, by provenance
print(ephysatlas.features.voltage_features_set())

# The frequency bands
print(ephysatlas.features.BANDS)

# Column names, dtypes, descriptions and units straight from the schema
schema = ephysatlas.features.ModelRawFeatures.to_schema()
for name, col in schema.columns.items():
    print(name, col.dtype, col.description, (col.metadata or {}).get("raw_unit"))
```

And when a model is involved, the model's own manifest is authoritative:

```python
from ephysatlas import load_pretrained

model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost", revision="2026_W42"
)
print(model.inputs["features"])   # exactly what this model needs, in order
```

## Which vintage changed what

Feature definitions change between vintages. `FEATURES_CHANGELOG.md` in the repository
root is the authoritative record; the headline changes:

| vintage | change |
|---|---|
| `2025_W28` | `rms_ap` / `rms_lf` denoised in dB and `spike_count` in log2, returned transformed. Channel `*_target` coordinates gained a 5° pitch correction |
| `2025_W39` | Added the spectral-parameterisation features (`aperiodic_*`, `decay_*`, `psd_residual_*`) |
| `2025_W43` | Bad-alpha filtering added to the aggregation pipeline |
| `2026_W39` | Computed with `ephysatlas` 0.9.0 (feature version `2026.09.20`): waveform amplitudes in volts, `spike_count` a rate, the denoised table remapped to the spike-shape columns, and the multi-channel `spatial_spread_um` / `slowness_s_per_m` features with their `_std` (listed in `FEATURES_CHANGELOG.md` under a provisional `2025_W51` heading) |
| `2026_W42` | The first-difference CSD columns renamed `*_csd_diff1` → `*_bpr`, and the CSD and BPR computed with the ibl-neuropixel 1.14 Cadzow denoising (Gavish-Donoho shrinkage, full grid for NP1), which changes their values |

See [core concepts](../explanation/concepts.qmd) for why a model and its features must
come from the same vintage.
